summary: Introduces a general mechanism for clients to discover optional LDAP features and extensions that cannot be discovered by existing means. This helps clients adapt to what a given server supports. It is a proposed standard that has been replaced by RFC 4512.

eli5.summary: Before asking a shopkeeper for a special item, you would like to know whether the shop has it. This lets a program ask a directory server what extra tricks it knows. RFC 4512 replaced it.

questions: how do ldap clients find server capabilities
subtitle: How LDAP clients can discover optional server features and extensions.

tldr.problem: LDAP is extensible with many optional features, but clients cannot always determine what features a given server supports using existing discovery mechanisms.
tldr.mechanism: A new supportedFeatures attribute in the root DSE (directory service entry) advertises features as Object Identifiers (OIDs). Clients query this attribute to check if a server supports specific features before attempting to use them.
tldr.outcome: Clients can now reliably discover optional LDAP features and adapt their behavior to what the server supports, avoiding failures from unsupported operations. RFC 4512 replaced this document.

today: RFC 3674 is Proposed Standard and was obsoleted by RFC 4512. The supportedFeatures attribute remains the standard way LDAP clients discover optional server capabilities.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is an extensible protocol with many optional features. While LDAP provides mechanisms to discover supported protocol versions, controls, extended operations, and authentication mechanisms, these do not support general feature discovery.

This document describes a simple mechanism that clients can use to discover the set of elective features supported by a server, allowing them to adapt their behavior accordingly.
sections.eli5: LDAP is a system for looking up information in a directory. Servers can support extra features, but the old ways of discovering them were not complete.

sections.title: Feature Discovery
sections.content:
Each elective feature is identified by an Object Identifier (OID). A server advertises support for a feature by providing the feature's OID as a value of the supportedFeatures attribute held in the root DSE (the top-level directory service entry).

A client may examine the values of this attribute to determine which features the server supports. A client MUST ignore values it does not recognize, as they refer to elective features the client does not implement.

Features associated with Standard Track protocol mechanisms MUST be registered with IANA. Features from other mechanisms SHOULD be registered. Procedures for registering protocol mechanisms are described in BCP 64 (RFC 3383).
sections.eli5: The server keeps a list of extra features it supports, marked by code numbers. When a client connects, it can look at this list to see what the server can do.

sections.title: The supportedFeatures Attribute
sections.content:
The supportedFeatures attribute type is defined with the OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.3.5. It contains Object Identifier values and uses the EQUALITY objectIdentifierMatch rule for comparison. The syntax is OID.

Servers MUST be capable of recognizing this attribute by the name 'supportedFeatures'. Servers MAY also recognize it by other names.

Examples of features that might be advertised include support for all operational attributes (RFC 3673) or support for true/false search filters.
sections.eli5: The server publishes an official list labeled "supportedFeatures" that contains code numbers for each extra thing it can do.
